settings.headline: Founded 1891, on the same hill
settings.subtitle: Tarrenhurst School is a fictional independent coeducational day school for 628 students from Pre-K to Grade 12, in the invented town of Tarrenhurst.

items.label: Acres, with woods and a stream

settings.headline: A short history
settings.body:
Josiah Ashby opened the school in 1891 with eleven pupils in a farmhouse. Agnes Thorne, the first headmistress, made it coeducational in 1902 and started the house system. The Tarren Building went up in 1928 and was rebuilt after the 1951 fire.

Today the school has three divisions on one campus, four houses and an archive that keeps every house cup ledger since 1903.
settings.note: Tarrenhurst School, its town, people, figures and history are invented for this Raytha example. Phone numbers use the 555 range.

settings.headline: What we believe
settings.body:
Children learn best when they are known. Small classes, advisors and houses exist so that every student has several adults who notice them.

We teach through conversation and making things, and we ask students to show their thinking, not just their answers.
settings.note: In the story, Tarrenhurst is accredited by a regional association of independent schools. This is a fictional statement.
